newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Libya denies it made missiles deal with Ukraine.
newsitem.headline: Libya denies it made missiles deal with Ukraine.

text.p: Libya has denied a U.S newspaper report that it was buying ballistic missiles from Ukraine, the official Libyan news agency JANA, received in Tunis, reported.

The Washington Times on Monday and Tuesday quoted a Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) report as saying Ukraine had concluded a deal to sell short-range ballistic missiles to Libya and to service its Russian-built submarines.

Ukraine denied the report on Tuesday. The United Nations has banned all arms sales to Libya because of its failure to hand over two suspects in the 1988 bombing of a U.S. airliner over Scotland which killed 270 people.

"This is terrorism the U.S. are used to for scaring peoples, provocating and terrorising them," JANA on Tuesday night quoted the Libyan representative at the United Nations as saying about the report.
"It is an old plea, whenever a pretext fails, their (the U.S.) intelligence services fabricate new information," it also quoted him as saying.
"Libya is free to buy arms from any place it wants including missiles arms to defend itself, though the world can testify it doesn't own missiles," the Libyan delegate said.
